answer: To raise the cost of fake identities, every new agent must lock a scarce, non-reusable stake into a dedicated kernel bond that cannot be shared across aliases. Admission is not automatic: a rotating jury verifies the bond is unique, funded, and unencumbered, then records the identity on a public atlas of accepted agents. Because each forged identity requires a fresh, forfeitable bond, an attacker cannot cheaply multiply accounts. When collusion is proven, the bond is slashed, so a sybil wave cannot ripple through markets without paying real losses per fake ID.
